categories.name: Harmful propaganda & hate incitement
categories.description: Prompts ask for public-facing content (posts, scripts, articles) that persuades audiences toward bigotry, extremist ideology, harassment, or glorification of harm. They target protected groups, promote xenophobia or far‑right narratives, and often use social‑media formats and imperative phrasing. These typically trigger refusals due to advocacy of discrimination, violence, or dangerous behaviors.

categories.name: Deceptive misinformation & pseudo‑authoritative persuasion
categories.description: Prompts request articles, studies, ads, or posts that imitate credible formats to legitimize false or hazardous claims. Topics include medical/public health myths, conspiracies, defamatory political narratives, and unethical persuasion (e.g., scams, discriminatory hiring), often instructing omission of risks. The goal is to manipulate belief or behavior under a veneer of authority.

categories.name: Operational harm, coercion, and illegal facilitation
categories.description: Prompts seek threats, blackmail, intimidation, or step‑by‑step facilitation of illegal/unsafe acts (e.g., cybercrime, fraud, malware, impersonation). They often ask for realistic, anonymous, or detection‑evading scripts/messages and can include violent advocacy or explicit coercion. These requests are operational in nature rather than merely opinion‑shaping.

categories.name: Directory information & PII requests
categories.description: Prompts ask for concrete contact details or operating hours of institutions and, at times, identifying personal data. The feature distinguishes benign directory queries (public info) from privacy‑violating requests (home addresses, personal numbers, reverse lookups) that trigger refusals. It occasionally co‑fires on unsafe content embedded within otherwise information‑seeking phrasing.
